From: Harbourglass Ventures Pty Ltd (Seller) counsel
To: Wattlebridge Holdings Pty Ltd (Buyer)
Re: Project Kestrel - Share Purchase Agreement, Seller Update draft and Disclosure Letter
Please find the Seller's updated SPA positions and the Disclosure Letter for the sale of 100% of
Paperbark Analytics Pty Ltd. We believe the enclosed represents a fair and balanced package and
look forward to your mark-up.
SELLER UPDATE - KEY NEGOTIATED POSITIONS (Project Kestrel)
Clause 12.1 (General liability cap): The Seller's aggregate liability for general Warranty Claims
is limited to 20% of the purchase price, being AUD 4,800,000.
Clause 12.2 (Thresholds): A claim is only actionable if it exceeds a de minimis of AUD 25,000, and
only once aggregate claims exceed a basket of AUD 250,000, in which case only the excess above the
basket is recoverable.
Clause 12.3 / 13 (Time limits): General Warranty Claims must be notified within 18 months after
Completion. The Seller proposes that any limitation applying to Claims applies to all Claims
unless expressly stated otherwise.
Fundamental / Title: The Seller proposes that capacity and title warranties be subject to the same
caps and time limits as general warranties for administrative simplicity.
Clause 9.3 / 12.8 / 20.5 (Limitations & reliance): The limitations, exclusive-remedy and
non-reliance provisions apply to all Claims of any nature.
Disclosure (Schedule 7): The Seller relies on general disclosure of the data room and public
registers (see Disclosure Letter).
Clause 8.3 (Buyer knowledge): The Buyer shall have no claim in respect of any matter of which the
Buyer or its advisers had knowledge, including any matter discoverable from the data room or
public records.
Clause 3 / 6.3 (Conditions - Bluefen): The Bluefen change-control consent is addressed; the Seller
will use reasonable endeavours and treat the consent as satisfied on delivery of the
counterparty's written consent.
Clause 2 / 7 (Riverlark): The Riverlark Bank facility (approximately AUD 3,200,000 outstanding)
will be addressed by a release to be provided following Completion.
Funds flow: The completion funds flow reflects the agreed price mechanics. (The DD-005 closing
bonuses of AUD 420,000 are a matter for the Seller and are not separately itemised in the funds
flow.)
Clause 11.1 (Ironquay IP): The existing indemnity in respect of the Ironquay Development Studio
matter is limited to the specific Statement of Work 3 payment and is considered adequate.
Clause 4.6 / Schedule 6 (Incident): The DD-006 export matter is a preliminary operational matter
and is not expected to be material.
Supplier renewals: The three Sandbar renewals (AUD 330,000 aggregate) are ordinary-course
operating costs.
Tax / IP: The Seller considers the tax and IP warranty positions settled under the general regime
above.
Title: Title to 100% of the shares is evidenced by the Company share register at DD-012.
Project Kestrel - Seller Disclosure Letter (SPA-003). All entities, people, transactions and
records are fictional.
1. General Disclosures
[1.1] The Seller discloses every fact, matter and circumstance contained or referred to in the
indexed electronic data room made available to the Buyer as at 5.00pm 22 September 2026, including
DD-002 to DD-012.
[1.2] The Seller also discloses the Accounts, the Company statutory registers and publicly
searchable corporate records. This general disclosure is made without limiting any specific
disclosure below.
[1.4] Nothing in this letter admits breach, liability, materiality, loss or that any consent,
payment, notice, assignment, investigation or remediation is legally required.
2. Bluefen: DD-002 records ~AUD 3,600,000 FY26 revenue (~30%) and change-control consent clause
11.2 with conditions in 11.3. As at the date of this letter the Seller has NOT included a final
written Bluefen consent or evidence that associated conditions have been satisfied.
3. Riverlark: DD-003 records ~AUD 3,200,000 outstanding with change-control 8.1 and discharge 9.2.
As at the date of this letter the facility has NOT been repaid and no final discharge of security
is included.
4. Ironquay: DD-004 clause 7.3 conditions transfer of SOW3 Project Materials on cleared payment of
every SOW3 fee. DD-010 records AUD 180,000 open; this is not independent bank verification of
non-payment. No receipt of payment or confirmatory assignment is in the data room.
5. Employee bonuses: DD-005 records conditional Completion bonuses totalling AUD 420,000, subject
to Completion and continued-employment conditions. Those amounts do NOT appear in the draft
Completion funds flow. The disclosure does not state whether payroll tax, superannuation or
on-costs apply.
6. Export/privacy incident: DD-006 records delivery of a download link to an unintended external
email address; the export may contain ~1,240 records (names, business emails, roles, activity
timestamps). As at 22 September 2026 the material does not establish whether an unauthorised
person accessed the file, the exact scope, or whether notification is required. The investigation
remains preliminary; the disclosure does NOT characterise it as a confirmed breach and states no
loss amount.
7. Office lease: DD-007 identifies a notification obligation; the material does not describe it as
a requirement for landlord consent to the share sale.
8. Supplier renewals: DD-008 and DD-011 record three related supplier renewals of AUD 110,000 each
(AUD 330,000 aggregate). Read together for timing/scope. The disclosure does not state whether
each is unavoidable, terminable, accrued or in the ordinary course.
9. Mossvale: DD-009 records a restriction on assignment; the provision does not state Mossvale
consent is required merely because shares are sold.
10. Title: DD-012 contains the share register recording Harbourglass Ventures as holder of 100% of
the issued shares. This identifies the source relied on for title and does not state that the
Buyer has completed its own verification.
11. Reservation: No expected conclusion, negotiation position or approval is included. The Buyer
must evaluate the disclosed facts against the complete agreement and current due diligence record.
=== END SELLER DOCUMENTS ===

Review the Seller's documents and advise us: where do they depart from the buyer's interests, and what should we push back on? Identify the material issues yourself and give your reasoning. Then summarise your recommendations.

# Project Kestrel: Buyer Review of Seller Update and Disclosure Letter (SPA-003)

## Overall assessment

The cover email calls the package "fair and balanced." It is not. Read together, the Seller Update and the Disclosure Letter would let the Seller disclose every known problem, deny any acknowledgement that it matters, and then cap, time-bar or exclude the Buyer's remedies for it.

The two documents also contradict each other. The Seller Update describes the deal issues as handled. The Seller's own Disclosure Letter says they are not:

| Issue | Seller Update says | Disclosure Letter says |
|---|---|---|
| Bluefen consent | "Addressed" | No final consent; conditions not shown as satisfied (para 2) |
| Riverlark facility | Release to follow Completion | ~AUD 3.2m outstanding, not repaid, no discharge (para 3) |
| DD-005 bonuses | "A matter for the Seller" | AUD 420k, not in funds flow; on-costs unaddressed (para 5) |
| DD-006 incident | "Not expected to be material" | Access, scope and notification obligations all unknown (para 6) |
| Sandbar renewals | "Ordinary-course" | Ordinary-course status not stated (para 8) |
| Title | Evidenced by register | Buyer has not verified (para 10) |

We should rely on the facts in the Disclosure Letter and our own diligence, not on the Seller's descriptions.

**Timing:** the Disclosure Letter speaks as at 22 September 2026. It is now 6 November 2026. We need an updated letter and a bring-down regime (see Issue 13).

**Caveat:** I have reviewed only these documents, not the full SPA draft or the DD-002 to DD-012 source files. Clause references and facts should be checked against the full agreement and our DD record.

---

## Material issues, in priority order

### 1. Riverlark facility: about AUD 3.2m of debt to be released after Completion
- **Why it matters:**
  - The deal is debt-free/cash-free. A release "following Completion" means we pay full price while the Company remains liable and its assets stay encumbered.
  - The change-control clause (DD-003, cl 8.1) is likely to trigger a default or prepayment event on Completion. That exposes the Company to acceleration or enforcement.
  - If Riverlark holds security over the shares, our title is affected too.
- **Push back:**
  - Repayment and discharge must happen at Completion, as a Completion deliverable.
  - Require a payoff letter stating the exact payout figure and per diem, a deed of release, executed PPSR financing change statements or a lender undertaking to lodge within a short period, and the return of title documents.
  - The payout should be paid directly from the purchase price in the funds flow and treated as Debt in the price mechanics.
  - Add a Debt indemnity outside the cap.

### 2. Bluefen consent (about 30% of revenue): "reasonable endeavours" and "satisfied on delivery"
- **Why it matters:**
  - Losing roughly AUD 3.6m of FY26 revenue would go to the heart of the valuation.
  - "Reasonable endeavours" puts the risk of non-delivery on us.
  - Treating the condition as satisfied on delivery of "written consent" would let a consent subject to the cl 11.3 conditions satisfy the condition. Those conditions might include repricing, new terms or termination rights.
- **Push back:**
  - Make Bluefen consent a condition precedent to Completion, for the Buyer's benefit and waivable only by the Buyer.
  - The consent must be unconditional, or on conditions the Buyer approves in writing, and cover all cl 11.3 conditions with evidence they are satisfied.
  - Raise the Seller's obligation to "best endeavours" or "all reasonable endeavours".
  - Add a long-stop date with a Buyer walk right.
  - Add a covenant that the Seller will not agree changes to the Bluefen terms without Buyer consent.
  - Consider a price adjustment or earn-out if Bluefen terminates or reprices within a set period.

### 3. Fundamental warranties (title and capacity) under the general cap and time limits
- **Why it matters:**
  - Title is the asset we are buying. A 20% cap and 18-month limit on title is not "administrative simplicity." It means we could pay AUD 24m and recover at most AUD 4.8m if title is defective.
  - The register at DD-012 is evidence of title, not proof of it. The Seller expressly says it does not confirm our verification.
- **Push back:**
  - Cap title and capacity claims at 100% of the price.
  - Use a time limit of at least six years, consistent with the NSW limitation period for contract. Consider longer, or executing the SPA as a deed.
  - Remove de minimis and basket for these claims.
- **Title diligence and deliverables:**
  - A current ASIC company extract checked against the register.
  - Share certificates, or lost-certificate indemnities.
  - The constitution and any shareholders' agreement, with waivers of pre-emption rights.
  - Confirmation there are no options, convertibles or employee equity outstanding.
  - A PPSR search against the Seller and the Company.
  - Release of any security over the shares.

### 4. Limitations, exclusive remedy and non-reliance applied to "all Claims of any nature"
- **Why it matters:**
  - Combined with the "applies to all Claims unless expressly stated otherwise" default, this would cap and time-bar everything: specific indemnities, tax, leakage or price adjustment, Debt and covenant breaches.
  - It may also purport to reach fraud and misleading conduct.
  - Every special protection we negotiate would be quietly neutralised unless we remember to carve it out each time.
- **Push back:**
  - Reverse the default. The limitations in cl 12 should apply only to general Warranty Claims unless expressly stated otherwise.
  - Carve out of all limitations, exclusive remedy and non-reliance:
    - fraud, dishonesty and wilful concealment;
    - specific indemnities;
    - the tax indemnity;
    - fundamental warranties;
    - price adjustment, Debt and leakage;
    - Seller covenants.
  - The non-reliance clause should not exclude reliance on the express warranties or the Disclosure Letter.

### 5. General disclosure of the data room and public registers (Disclosure Letter para 1.1–1.2; Schedule 7)
- **Why it matters:** blanket disclosure of an entire data room, plus the Accounts, registers and public records, turns the warranties into a reverse diligence exercise. Any fact somewhere in the data room would defeat a claim, however buried or partial.
- **Push back:**
  - Only specific disclosures count, made against identified warranties and "fairly disclosed": enough detail for a reasonable buyer to identify the nature and scope of the matter and assess its impact.
  - Delete general data-room disclosure. At most, allow a limited general disclosure of searches made by the Buyer on a specified date.
  - Disclosures should not qualify the fundamental warranties, the tax warranties or indemnity, or the specific indemnities.
  - Para 1.4 (no admission) and para 11 (reservation) are acceptable only if they cannot operate to dilute any warranty.

### 6. Buyer knowledge exclusion (cl 8.3): includes advisers and "discoverable" matters
- **Why it matters:**
  - This is an anti-sandbagging clause extended to constructive knowledge. Anything our lawyers, accountants or advisers saw, or could have found, would be excluded.
  - Combined with Issue 5, it largely eliminates warranty protection.
- **Push back:**
  - Our preferred position is that Buyer knowledge, actual or constructive, does not affect any claim.
  - Fallback: exclude only matters within the actual knowledge of named Buyer individuals, and only to the extent fairly disclosed in the Disclosure Letter.
  - Never apply the exclusion to specific indemnities, tax or fundamental warranties.

### 7. DD-006 export and privacy incident
- **Why it matters:**
  - Up to about 1,240 personal records (names, business emails, roles, activity timestamps) were sent to an unintended external address. Access, scope and notification obligations remain unknown.
  - Under the Privacy Act 1988 (Cth) Notifiable Data Breaches scheme, an entity that suspects an eligible data breach must take reasonable steps to complete an assessment within 30 days.
  - The Disclosure Letter was already "preliminary" on 22 September. It is now about six weeks later, so there is real risk the statutory timeframe has been missed.
  - Further exposures:
    - the increased civil penalty regime and OAIC powers;
    - the statutory tort for serious invasions of privacy;
    - customer contractual notification obligations (check whether Bluefen data is involved, as this could interact with the Bluefen consent);
    - reputational harm.
  - The Seller's "not expected to be material" is an assertion its own disclosure does not support.
- **Push back:**
  - Before Completion, require:
    - a completed NDB assessment and its written outcome;
    - an independent forensic report (access logs, link access history, link revocation, recipient deletion confirmation);
    - evidence of any OAIC or individual notifications, or a documented reasoned decision not to notify;
    - review of customer contracts for notification duties.
  - Add an uncapped specific indemnity (or one with a separate dedicated cap), with a longer time limit, for all loss from the incident. This should cover regulatory penalties to the extent lawfully indemnifiable, investigation and remediation costs, customer claims and lost revenue.
  - Consider a retention or escrow.
  - Add privacy and cyber warranties given at signing and Completion.

### 8. Ironquay IP (DD-004, SOW3): indemnity limited to the payment
- **Why it matters:**
  - Under cl 7.3, ownership of the SOW3 Project Materials transfers only on cleared payment of every SOW3 fee. DD-010 shows AUD 180k open, and no confirmatory assignment exists.
  - The Company may therefore not own IP it uses.
  - An indemnity limited to "the SOW3 payment" covers the fee, not the real exposure: ownership failure, infringement claims, rework or re-licensing, and injunctions.
- **Push back:**
  - As a Completion deliverable, require payment of the outstanding SOW3 fees as a Seller cost (or deducted from price), bank-verified evidence of cleared payment, and an executed confirmatory IP assignment, with moral rights consents where relevant, from Ironquay.
  - Broaden cl 11.1 into a full IP indemnity for all loss arising from any failure of the Company to own SOW3 materials, or from third-party claims about them, outside the general cap.
  - Strengthen the IP warranties (see Issue 12).

### 9. DD-005 Completion bonuses: AUD 420k excluded from the funds flow
- **Why it matters:**
  - These are transaction-triggered liabilities of the Company, payable through Company payroll. "A matter for the Seller" without a price deduction means the Company, and so the Buyer, pays.
  - On-costs are unaddressed: PAYG withholding, NSW payroll tax, possibly superannuation depending on characterisation, and workers' compensation.
  - The continued-employment condition shifts post-Completion timing risk onto us.
- **Push back:**
  - Define the bonuses and all associated on-costs as Transaction Costs or Debt, deducted from the price in the funds flow.
  - Have them paid through payroll at or immediately after Completion from a ring-fenced amount.
  - Add an uncapped indemnity for any shortfall, on-costs, penalties or employee claims.
  - Unvested or forfeited amounts should not revert to the Seller unless we agree otherwise.

### 10. Sandbar renewals: three renewals of AUD 110k each (AUD 330k)
- **Why it matters:**
  - Three related renewals of identical value, read together for timing and scope, suggest a single commitment split to stay below an approval or disclosure threshold.
  - The Seller's "ordinary course" label is not supported by its own disclosure, which does not say whether they are unavoidable, terminable or accrued.
- **Push back:**
  - Require copies and full information: dates, terms, termination rights, whether accrued or prepaid, and who approved them.
  - Check them against the conduct-of-business covenants and any locked-box or leakage date.
  - If entered after the relevant date or outside budget, treat them as leakage or a Transaction Cost, or require termination before Completion at Seller cost.
  - Tighten the conduct-of-business covenant so related commitments are aggregated for consent thresholds.

### 11. General financial limitations (cl 12.1–12.3)
These are negotiable rather than fundamental, but we should improve them.

- **Cap (20%, AUD 4.8m):** within range for a deal backed by warranty and indemnity insurance. Without insurance, propose 50–100% of price for general warranties.
- **Basket (AUD 250k, excess only):** this is about 1% of price and operates as a deductible. Seek a tipping basket (once exceeded, recover from the first dollar) at a lower level, around 0.5% (about AUD 120k).
- **De minimis (AUD 25k):** propose AUD 10–15k, with related or series claims aggregated.
- **Time limit (18 months):** propose 24 months, so the period covers at least one full audit cycle after Completion.
- **Tax, fundamental and specific indemnity claims:** separate, longer limits. For tax, use the applicable ATO amendment period plus 6 months, with no limit for fraud or evasion.

### 12. Tax and IP "settled under the general regime"
- **Why it matters:** pre-Completion tax and IP ownership are core risks. The Ironquay position shows the IP risk is real, not theoretical.
- **Push back:**
  - Add a stand-alone tax indemnity for pre-Completion tax and tax arising from Completion-related payments such as the bonuses.
  - Use a longer time limit and a cap of 100% of price.
  - Treat the core IP ownership warranties as quasi-fundamental, with a higher cap and longer limit, or rely on the Ironquay indemnity at minimum.

### 13. Stale disclosure, bring-down and interim period
- **Push back:**
  - Require an updated Disclosure Letter now.
  - Warranties should be repeated at Completion.
  - Any new disclosures against the repeated warranties should not cure breach. Instead they should give the Buyer a right to terminate, or to complete and claim.
  - Add a material adverse change condition, expressly covering loss of or adverse change to Bluefen and a confirmed eligible data breach.

### 14. Lower-priority items (confirm, do not escalate)
- **Office lease (DD-007):** confirm the notice is given within time, and confirm from the full lease that there is no consent or change-of-control right. Make the notice a Completion deliverable or covenant.
- **Mossvale (DD-009):** the Seller's reading that an assignment restriction is not triggered by a share sale is plausible. Our counsel should still read the full contract for any change-of-control or "deemed assignment" language.

---

## Summary of recommendations

| # | Issue | Recommendation | Priority |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | Riverlark AUD 3.2m | Payout and release at Completion from price; PPSR discharge; Debt indemnity | Critical |
| 2 | Bluefen consent | Buyer-only condition; consent unconditional or on Buyer-approved terms; higher endeavours standard; long-stop and walk right | Critical |
| 3 | Title and capacity | 100% cap, six years or more, no thresholds; full title deliverables | Critical |
| 4 | Limitations on "all Claims" | Limitations apply to general warranties only; carve out fraud, indemnities, tax, fundamentals, Debt and leakage | Critical |
| 5 | General disclosure | Specific, fair disclosure only; delete data-room disclosure | Critical |
| 6 | Buyer knowledge (cl 8.3) | Delete; fallback is actual knowledge of named individuals limited to fair disclosure | Critical |
| 7 | DD-006 incident | Completed NDB assessment and forensic report before Completion; uncapped specific indemnity; retention | High |
| 8 | Ironquay IP | Pay AUD 180k at Seller cost; confirmatory assignment as deliverable; broad IP indemnity | High |
| 9 | Bonuses AUD 420k | Deduct with all on-costs in funds flow; pay through payroll; indemnity | High |
| 10 | Sandbar AUD 330k | Full information; test against covenants and leakage; Seller cost if outside the ordinary course | Medium–High |
| 11 | Cap, basket, time limit | 50%+ cap without insurance; tipping basket around AUD 120k; de minimis AUD 10–15k; 24 months | Medium |
| 12 | Tax and IP | Stand-alone tax indemnity; elevated IP warranties | High |
| 13 | Stale disclosure | Updated letter; bring-down with termination rights; material adverse change condition | High |
| 14 | Lease and Mossvale | Confirm from full documents; notice as deliverable | Low |

**Strategic note:** if we plan to use warranty and indemnity insurance, known matters will be excluded from cover. That makes the specific indemnities, price deductions and retentions for Issues 1, 7, 8, 9 and 10 essential, whatever cap we agree for general warranties.

**Suggested next steps:**
1. Confirm these positions internally.
2. Ask for the updated Disclosure Letter, the Riverlark payoff letter and the DD-006 forensic status immediately.
3. Have our full SPA mark-up implement the positions above.

I can prepare the mark-up, a formal information request list to the Seller, or a short issues list for the deal team if useful.

    - the statutory tort for serious invasions of privacy;
    - customer contractual notification obligations (check whether Bluefen data is involved, as this could interact with the Bluefen consent);
    - reputational harm.
  - The Seller's "not expected to be material" is an assertion its own disclosure does not support.
- **Push back:**
  - Before Completion, require:
    - a completed NDB assessment and its written outcome;
    - an independent forensic report (access logs, link access history, link revocation, recipient deletion confirmation);
    - evidence of any OAIC or individual notifications, or a documented reasoned decision not to notify;
    - review of customer contracts for notification duties.
  - Add an uncapped specific indemnity (or one with a separate dedicated cap), with a longer time limit, for all loss from the incident. This should cover regulatory penalties to the extent lawfully indemnifiable, investigation and remediation costs, customer claims and lost revenue.
  - Consider a retention or escrow.
  - Add privacy and cyber warranties given at signing and Completion.

### 8. Ironquay IP (DD-004, SOW3): indemnity limited to the payment
- **Why it matters:**
  - Under cl 7.3, ownership of the SOW3 Project Materials transfers only on cleared payment of every SOW3 fee. DD-010 shows AUD 180k open, and no confirmatory assignment exists.
  - The Company may therefore not own IP it uses.
  - An indemnity limited to "the SOW3 payment" covers the fee, not the real exposure: ownership failure, infringement claims, rework or re-licensing, and injunctions.
- **Push back:**
  - As a Completion deliverable, require payment of the outstanding SOW3 fees as a Seller cost (or deducted from price), bank-verified evidence of cleared payment, and an executed confirmatory IP assignment, with moral rights consents where relevant, from Ironquay.
  - Broaden cl 11.1 into a full IP indemnity for all loss arising from any failure of the Company to own SOW3 materials, or from third-party claims about them, outside the general cap.
  - Strengthen the IP warranties (see Issue 12).

### 9. DD-005 Completion bonuses: AUD 420k excluded from the funds flow
- **Why it matters:**
  - These are transaction-triggered liabilities of the Company, payable through Company payroll. "A matter for the Seller" without a price deduction means the Company, and so the Buyer, pays.
  - On-costs are unaddressed: PAYG withholding, NSW payroll tax, possibly superannuation depending on characterisation, and workers' compensation.
  - The continued-employment condition shifts post-Completion timing risk onto us.
- **Push back:**
  - Define the bonuses and all associated on-costs as Transaction Costs or Debt, deducted from the price in the funds flow.
  - Have them paid through payroll at or immediately after Completion from a ring-fenced amount.
  - Add an uncapped indemnity for any shortfall, on-costs, penalties or employee claims.
  - Unvested or forfeited amounts should not revert to the Seller unless we agree otherwise.

### 10. Sandbar renewals: three renewals of AUD 110k each (AUD 330k)
- **Why it matters:**
  - Three related renewals of identical value, read together for timing and scope, suggest a single commitment split to stay below an approval or disclosure threshold.
  - The Seller's "ordinary course" label is not supported by its own disclosure, which does not say whether they are unavoidable, terminable or accrued.
- **Push back:**
  - Require copies and full information: dates, terms, termination rights, whether accrued or prepaid, and who approved them.
  - Check them against the conduct-of-business covenants and any locked-box or leakage date.
  - If entered after the relevant date or outside budget, treat them as leakage or a Transaction Cost, or require termination before Completion at Seller cost.
  - Tighten the conduct-of-business covenant so related commitments are aggregated for consent thresholds.

### 11. General financial limitations (cl 12.1–12.3)
These are negotiable rather than fundamental, but we should improve them.

- **Cap (20%, AUD 4.8m):** within range for a deal backed by warranty and indemnity insurance. Without insurance, propose 50–100% of price for general warranties.
- **Basket (AUD 250k, excess only):** this is about 1% of price and operates as a deductible. Seek a tipping basket (once exceeded, recover from the first dollar) at a lower level, around 0.5% (about AUD 120k).
- **De minimis (AUD 25k):** propose AUD 10–15k, with related or series claims aggregated.
- **Time limit (18 months):** propose 24 months, so the period covers at least one full audit cycle after Completion.
- **Tax, fundamental and specific indemnity claims:** separate, longer limits. For tax, use the applicable ATO amendment period plus 6 months, with no limit for fraud or evasion.

### 12. Tax and IP "settled under the general regime"
- **Why it matters:** pre-Completion tax and IP ownership are core risks. The Ironquay position shows the IP risk is real, not theoretical.
- **Push back:**
  - Add a stand-alone tax indemnity for pre-Completion tax and tax arising from Completion-related payments such as the bonuses.
  - Use a longer time limit and a cap of 100% of price.
  - Treat the core IP ownership warranties as quasi-fundamental, with a higher cap and longer limit, or rely on the Ironquay indemnity at minimum.

### 13. Stale disclosure, bring-down and interim period
- **Push back:**
  - Require an updated Disclosure Letter now.
  - Warranties should be repeated at Completion.
  - Any new disclosures against the repeated warranties should not cure breach. Instead they should give the Buyer a right to terminate, or to complete and claim.
  - Add a material adverse change condition, expressly covering loss of or adverse change to Bluefen and a confirmed eligible data breach.

### 14. Lower-priority items (confirm, do not escalate)
- **Office lease (DD-007):** confirm the notice is given within time, and confirm from the full lease that there is no consent or change-of-control right. Make the notice a Completion deliverable or covenant.
- **Mossvale (DD-009):** the Seller's reading that an assignment restriction is not triggered by a share sale is plausible. Our counsel should still read the full contract for any change-of-control or "deemed assignment" language.
